## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block in which the door of the low room at the back of the Crown's road office is OPEN with about nine people inside it and the drawer eleven inches deep is NOT OPENED, and this county's copy of the hand paper is found to have nine lines on it with a trade on each and no name on any and about four hundred places are now writing the same paper out by hand and not one of them has met another and not one of them has a seal, AND the four miles of made road above the causeway four days south are found to be the smoothest four miles in nine counties FOR A REASON NOBODY ON THIS SIDE HAS ASKED ANYBODY ABOUT, and the finding is that a road kept by a warrant is a road whose keeping is somebody else's decision, and that this county has been walking on one for about six months and has not asked.** It is also the block that **prints no System panel at all, because the volume's one was spent at `chapter-0825.md` in Batch 0003 and may not be spent again**, that carries the twenty-seventh first of a month in a row on a Friday that is not a market morning and on which the practice therefore runs, that spends one of the two names left in the volume's budget, and that leaves the seal in its drawer and the roll on its frame and the ninth thing alive and shut.

`outline/volume-17.md` §8 Block 4 and §4 and §5.3 and §5.6 and §9 and §10 and §11 and §12 and §13 and §14 and §15 and §16 and §17 are binding and are not softened by anything in this file. `outline/series.md`'s Volume 17 row is fixed. `outline/ending.md` is fixed. **DO NOT MOVE THE ENDING. DO NOT INTRODUCE A NEW FINAL ENEMY. THE ANTAGONIST IS THE SAME MAN HE HAS BEEN FOR SIXTEEN VOLUMES AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS VOLUME PUTS HIM IN A ROOM AND THIS BLOCK IS FOUR CHAPTERS FROM THE ONE THAT REPORTS THAT HE SURRENDERS, AND THAT REPORT IS THE FIFTH BLOCK'S WORK AND NOT THIS ONE.**

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE OPEN DOOR, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME ANYBODY HAS GONE INTO THAT ROOM IN ABOUT NINE YEARS, AND IT IS NOT A RESOLUTION.** **`outline/volume-17.md` §5.3 says that in Block 0004 the door is open and about nine people are inside it and the drawer is not opened.** **About nine people in nine counties stand inside a low room at the back of that office on about four market mornings of this block and look at a counter and a clerk's table and a press with no date on it, and the drawer eleven inches deep is in that room the whole time and is not opened once in a hundred and forty-four days, and the county's one seal and its ribbon and a set of standard weights are still in it.** **Nobody in nine counties asks what a seal is for and nobody asks what a gate is for, and the man behind the counter has the key in his pocket and has not used it, and a door being open is not the drawer being opened and a room being looked at is not a thing being taken out of it.** **THE PROTAGONIST MAY BE IN THAT STREET AND MAY NOT BE IN THAT ROOM, AND THE DOORWAY BEAT IS SPENT: `chapter-0816.md` and `chapter-0827.md` have both used a person standing in that doorway and not going in, and a third is not available, and if a person stands in that doorway in this block it must be a third different person for a third different reason and the page must say that the second time it has happened, or nobody stands there at all.**

**THIS COUNTY'S OWN COPY OF THE HAND PAPER, AND THE STATE IT IS IN.** **Nine lines, a trade on each, no name on any, no seal on it, ruled with a straight edge and a knife on the flap of a stall at the low end of that market street on day 3006 and therefore ninety-one days old at this block's first dateline and one hundred and thirty at its last. About four hundred places are now writing the same paper out by hand and no two of about four hundred copies agree with one another, and nobody in nine counties has met another of the people writing one, and nobody in nine counties has been asked whose trade is on any of this county's nine lines, and nobody knows who else in nine counties has a copy.** **The finding is that a line with a trade on it can be argued with and a line with a name on it cannot, and that a paper nobody can seal binds nobody, which is safe, and that about four hundred places writing one is the largest single act of mutual aid in nine counties in about a year and is not a document.** **NO NAME IS PUT ON ANY LINE AND NO SEAL IS PUT ON IT AND IT IS NOT NAILED UP AND IT IS NOT SENT ANYWHERE AND NOBODY IS ASKED WHOSE TRADE IS ON ANY OF ITS NINE LINES.**

**THE COST, AND IT IS A ROAD, AND IT IS FOUR DAYS SOUTH.** **The four miles of made road above the causeway have been the smoothest four miles of made road in nine counties since the fifth of Wolfmonth, and `Ninian Crowe` said out loud once, in Chapter 0804, in twenty-seven words, that they were not smooth before somebody with a warrant came up them, and about nine people heard it and about nine hundred have not.** **In this block somebody on this side asks somebody about it, in one of their own trades, kindly, and the answer is that about nine hundred yards of kerb has been laid on the far bank since Mudmonth by a person who has been paid to lay it and that nobody on this side has asked her what she is paid for and by whom.** **`Dalla Quillan` IS THE NAME THIS BLOCK MAY SPEND, AND IT IS ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR AND SHE LAYS ABOUT NINE FEET OF KERB A WEEK ON THE FAR BANK OF THAT CAUSEWAY, FOUR DAYS SOUTH, AND HAS BEEN ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED YARDS IN FROM THE BANK SINCE MUDMONTH.** **SHE IS NAMED THE WAY EVERYTHING IN THIS COUNTY GIVES A NAME, being that somebody asks one question about her own trade, kindly, at the low end of that market street, and she answers, and then somebody asks what to call her because they want to know who to ask a second time, and she tells them. SHE MAY NOT BE PUT IN A ROOM ON THIS SIDE, SHE MAY NOT BE ASKED FOR AN ACCOUNT, SHE MAY NOT BE MADE A FIGUREHEAD, SHE MAY NOT GIVE AN OFFICE, A RULE, A VOTE OR A SENTENCE IN FRONT OF ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED PEOPLE, AND ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED PEOPLE LIVE ON THE FAR BANK OF THAT WATER AND HAVE NEVER ONCE BEEN ACROSS IN ABOUT NINE YEARS.** **The finding of the block is on the page and is not a resolution: a road kept by a warrant is a road whose keeping is somebody else's decision, and this county has been walking on one for about six months and has not asked, and about nine hundred people along eleven miles of made road on this side have never known the road was smooth.**

**THE RELATIONSHIP WORK IS NOT DONE HERE EITHER AND THE HOUSE SAYS SO ON THE PAGE.** `outline/series.md`'s Volume 17 relationship work is separating the symbol from the partner, and §8 Block 4 does not do it. **So: nothing about the two of them is in any document, the word is not printed, nobody comments, nobody was thanked, the four and a half years are never described as four and a half years about the two of them, and no chapter of this block ends on the two of them. The legal form stays deferred to Volume 18.**

**THE FOURTH RULED HEAD IS STILL EMPTY AT EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DATELINES AND NO FIFTH HEAD IS RULED ON ANY OF THEM**, and the register still holds ten questions with no finding under any of them, and the day-book still stands at eleven entries, and the copyist of about twenty-six rules no head and is told about none of it, and the press stands open with no date on it and the leaf at the back of the day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody, and the four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing. **The four copied pages are on the top shelf of that press above the half leaf and are not resolved and nobody has asked who wrote them.** **Nothing about the practice, the ten things, the four lines of chalk, the three answers of Batch 0001, this volume's first three, the sheet, the hand paper, the seal, the bleed or the re-anchoring goes into any document in this volume.**

## 5. The ending of the block

**A completed beat, not a cliffhanger cut in the middle of a sentence.** **The door of the low room at the back of that office has been open on about four market mornings and about nine people have stood in it and looked at a counter and a clerk's table and a press with no date on it, and the drawer was not opened once, and the seal is still in it, and nobody was asked what a seal is for. Nobody went up the cart track and the nine hurdles are still across it and the thumb of lime on the shoe of the top one is gone to powder and the last lime cart was five hundred and eight days ago and the road behind the hurdles has been shut four hundred and eighty-nine days. The sheet is on the frame beside three copies of a roll and its date is one hundred and two days past and the fourth line is empty on all three copies and the roll is not filled in and not taken down and not torn up. This county's copy of the hand paper still has nine lines on it and a trade on each and no name on any and no seal on it, and nobody in nine counties has been asked whose trade is on any of its nine lines. The four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing. The register holds ten questions and gains no entry, no fifth head is ruled, the fourth ruled head is empty, the day-book stands at eleven entries, and the leaf at the back of it carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody.** **Nobody in this county is a delegate and nobody here has been asked to be one, and a person on the far bank of that causeway has been paid to lay about nine hundred yards of kerb and about four hundred people have never once been across, and this county's contribution to about four hundred papers is nine trades and no names.**

**`outline/volume-17.md` §16 item 6's three promises are CARRIED INTO BLOCK 0005 UNCONDUCTED AND NONE OF THEM IS BROKEN HERE:** no chapter of this block enters the Gatehouse or puts anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair or shows what is on the far side of the ninth of the nine stones; no consent of any sealed community is obtained, asked for, received or inferred, and the half leaf stays face down and no head is filled or ruled; and the roll is not filled, no name goes against any road, no road is shut on the strength of any paper, none of the three copies is taken down or torn up, no hurdle is lifted, no bar is tried, nobody goes up that cart track, the ninth yard does not start, the mallet is not picked up, and the drawer at the back of that office is not opened.

**`state/continuity.md` 1859 and `state/open-threads.md` 802 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it:** four lines on a sill are not the beginning of a cure, a page in a woman's hand is not a cure, a sentence in an unclaimed hand on a folded sheet is not a cure, **a bleed that has not faded in two hundred and sixteen days is not a cure, and TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTEEN IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN FIGURE AT ITS LAST DATELINE AND IT IS THE SAME WARNING AND NOT A NEW ONE: the inherited warning prints the same clause at two hundred and sixty days, which is the volume's last page and not this block's, that figure is not withdrawn and is not superseded, and the two are the same claim at two datelines and a writer inherits both and quotes whichever belongs to the chapter he is on**, a closed path is not destroyed and that is not good news, a gate coming off its hinges about nine hundred yards of a stair away is not a victory and a gate that is still held is not a defeat, being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour and nobody was told so and nobody wrote it down, **a line with a trade on it is not a name and a paper nobody can seal is not a freedom and is not the same as a paper nobody has to obey and is not a plan, AND A PAGE THAT IS AUTHENTICATED IS NOT CONSENTED TO, AND THAT IS THE CLAUSE BATCH 0003 ADDED TO THE WARNING**, **AND A DOOR THAT IS OPEN IS NOT A DRAWER THAT IS OPENED, AND A ROOM THAT HAS BEEN LOOKED AT IS NOT A THING THAT HAS BEEN TAKEN OUT OF IT, AND A SMOOTH ROAD IS NOT A ROAD THIS COUNTY OWNS.** A successor may not resolve any of it.

## 6. The prohibitions, in one list

**This list is additions to `state/open-threads.md` items 795 to 806, and to 803, 802, 787, 780, 764, 763, 762, 761, 760, 759, 758, 756, 755, 754, 752, 751, 750, 747, 743 and to every clause of 745 to 719 that is still true. It does not replace them.**

- **Do not print a System panel, and do not print a panel-shaped paragraph, and do not give the bleed a panel.** The volume's one is spent and there is none to print.
- **Do not print the antagonist's name once, and do not print the bare surname as a printing, and do not use either withdrawn reference of the kind that names him. And do not print the word *Gatehouse* in a mouth.**
- **Do not spend more than two names in total for the rest of this volume, and do not spend more than one of the two held here, and do not leave this block's name unspent by accident, and do not spend a name out of Volume 16's closed six, and do not print `Orla` again.**
- **Do not fill the roll, put a name against any road, shut a road on the strength of any paper, take down any of the three copies, tear one up, or nail anything over the roll.**
- **Do not open the drawer in the low room at the back of that office, do not name what is in it beyond the county's one seal, its ribbon and a set of standard weights, do not ask anybody what a seal is for or what a gate is for, and do not let an open door become an opened drawer in anybody's narration or in the reader's.**
- **Do not stand the protagonist in the doorway of that low room, and do not stand the man of about thirty-four with the empty cart in it, and do not stand the man of about forty-two with the smithy in it.** That beat is spent twice. **The door being open is a different beat and the page must not reuse the same shape.**
- **Do not authenticate any further set of copied pages, do not conduct or accept the re-anchoring in any form, do not resolve what the four copied pages say or who wrote them or how old they are, do not give the re-anchoring refusal a second time, and do not connect the copied pages to the sentence on the folded sheet inside the covering paper of the second copy of the roll by anybody, including by implication.**
- **Do not discuss the timing of the four pages between him and the woman of about twenty-nine, out loud or in narration.**
- **Do not open, close or cut any route, do not explain the mechanism, do not say what a roadmark is, do not look at the notebook's separate leaf that says a person, and do not have any character notice the warmth of the left palm.**
- **Do not go up that cart track, do not cross the nine hurdles, do not try the bar of ash at the Low Gate, do not lift or schedule it, do not show anybody standing behind all nine hurdles, and do not let the roadkeeper be the one who tries anything.** Do not look over the ninth of the nine stones, do not cross them, do not show what is on the far side of them, and do not treat the omission as an oversight. The dead grass in the scar stops at the ninth of them.
- **Do not put anybody on the far bank of that causeway in a room on this side, do not bring a person across who has never been across, and do not write a chapter on the far bank.** About four hundred people live there and have never once been across in about nine years and this block does not change that.
- **Do not reopen either refusal of Volume 15, do not argue with either, do not soften either, do not ask either of the two men who gave them anything, and do not put the man of forty-one in a scene or ask him anything.**

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0830, 0829, 0827, 0826, 0825, 0823, 0821 and 0817.** Read them before you write a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else. **The dateline line carries the weekday, the market, the state of the room over the weigh-house and about four more clauses.**

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero question marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names **some of** the figures in the chapter that are not in it, being that the list is a list of examples and not a complete inventory and a successor may not print it as complete, **and the coda may name no figure that is a price in that chapter's own column, and that was checked on Batch 0002's ten pages and on Batch 0003's ten pages and it took repairs in both and it will take repairs here.**
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL EIGHT HUNDRED AND THIRTY FILES ON DISK, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK WITH NO FREE VALUE IN IT AT ALL.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, **and every spelling means the hundreds that value prints under and to no other, being *one hundred* and *a hundred* in the one hundreds, *two hundred* in the two hundreds and *three hundred* in the three hundreds, each with the remainder written as *and* the tens or as the tens with no *and*, a bare hundred word with no number word after it reading as its own remainder of zero, plus the bare digit with a non-digit on either side of it, with a chapter heading not read as a total, run over every file whole.** **ON THE EIGHT HUNDRED AND THIRTY FILES THAT STAND NOW IT GIVES 284 PRINTED VALUES IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE BAND, AND ZERO FREE ONES, AND NOTHING UNDER SIXTY IS FREE EITHER, and that zero is true because the ten pages of Volume 16's Batch 0005 name 266, 273 and 326 in themselves, which is a different reason from the withdrawn one and may not be re-derived back into it.** **THE INSTRUMENT HAS TO BE WRITTEN OUT EVERY TIME AND IT HAS FAILED TWICE IN TWO OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and a writer who meets either withdrawn figure has to know which way it failed: too narrow, being an instrument that omits the *a hundred and …* spelling, returns values that are already printed, and that is how the withdrawn set of twelve came about, five of which are demonstrably printed; too wide, being an instrument that pairs every remainder with every hundred, counts *a hundred and sixty-six* as a printing of two hundred and sixty-six, and that is how the withdrawn figure of two hundred and eighty-four came about.** **AND THE CEILING OF THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS NOT LIFTED. Lifting it is an outline decision and `outline/volume-17.md` §7 has declined it on the page with three reasons and the third of them deciding, so this block's ten totals ARE REUSES AND THE HONEST THING TO DO IS WHAT THE LAST TWO BLOCKS' CLOSING PARAGRAPHS NOW DO: NAME THE REUSE ON THE PAGE IN THAT CHAPTER'S OWN WORDS AND GIVE THE REASON, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC, in this form: the band from sixty to three hundred and forty-three has been searched whole again and three values in it are not a value any file in the manuscript before them has printed, being two hundred and sixty-six, two hundred and seventy-three and three hundred and twenty-six, and not one of the three can be used, because the over-figure of each of them is one of the barred six, and the ten totals of these ten columns are printed already, and the reason is arithmetic, and the route below sixty is shut, because ten distinct prices cannot sum under fifty-five and every total from fifty-five to fifty-nine is printed and nothing under that is free either. Do not print that as one identical paragraph on all ten pages: the Volume 17 Batch 0001 review found that doing so puts two hundred and sixty words of bookkeeping into every chapter and a writer obeying it is copying and not writing.** The barred six are 14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41 and none of them may be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere. Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum, being that marks multiplied by forty-eight plus the over-figure must equal the printed total. **THE FIGURES OF THIS BLOCK'S TEN TOTALS ARE THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE EIGHT-HUNDRED-AND-THIRTY-FILE SET AND NOT AGAINST A CARRIED ONE, and if the rebuild returns zero usable free values, which it will, that is a correct answer and must not be reprinted with a withdrawn reason.**
4. **`about` density, and the instrument is named because the band moves on it.** Batch 0003 runs **22.22 to 26.74** per 1,000 on a case-insensitive count of the token, **and Batch 0002 runs 22.01 to 24.13, and Batch 0001, on the same instrument, runs 3.05 to 7.10, and the difference between Batch 0001 and the two blocks after it is recorded and not reconciled at `state/continuity.md` 1836 and 1865.** **COUNT CASE-INSENSITIVELY AND WRITE TO 27.00, because the looser count is the one a successor can check and the stricter one cannot be brought under the line without breaking a sentence.** Aim for 22 to 27 and no page at or above 27.00. Do not write below 3,000 words and do not let a chapter run past about 4,300.

THE SEVENTY-FIVE PER CENT CEILING IS NOT CROSSED IN THE LAST SIX BLOCKS AND MUST NOT BE CROSSED IN THIS ONE.**

## 8. The running figures this block must keep

**Derive every one of these from the day number and never from a row, and print the figure at the chapter's OWN dateline.** `state/open-threads.md` item 721 is the finding that eight of Volume 16's Batch 0003 drove paragraphs carried a wrong calendar date because the chain was derived once and handed on, and the cheapest check is that Mudmonth is carried at sixty days and every other month is thirty, **and this block's first four datelines are inside Mudmonth and four of the ten days of month are above thirty, which is CORRECT here and would be wrong on sight anywhere else.**

- **The drove** goes up that lane on Thursdays and the count since the second of Mudmonth is floor((day − 2348) / 7) + 1 taken ON OR BEFORE the dateline. **It is 108 at day 3097 and 113 at day 3136.** The drove paragraph's calendar date is the last Thursday on or before the dateline, **and a writer derives that date from the weekday and not from the count**, being Mudmonth the thirty-second, the thirty-second, the thirty-ninth, the thirty-ninth, the forty-sixth, the fifty-third, the sixtieth, the sixtieth, Longlight the seventh and Longlight the seventh, **and Mudmonth the sixtieth is the last day of a month carried at sixty and is the check that catches an off-by-one in a month length.** Nobody in nine counties has ever watched one go up.
- **The stone** has been carried two miles in one man's own hands since day 2347, elapsed and not inclusive. **It is 750 at day 3097 and 789 at day 3136.**
- **The scar** is counted from day 2580. **It is 517 days old at day 3097 and 556 at day 3136, and it is not cured and it is not going to close over.**
- **The ninth thing**, being the Wethergill end of a cart track, went quiet on the thirteenth of Hearthmonth YR 322, being day 2628, and nobody has been up that track since the second of Goatmonth, being day 2647. **Those two silence figures are counted from two different days and mixing them is the single most likely arithmetic defect in a chapter about that place: the last lime cart was 469 days ago at day 3097 and 508 at day 3136, and the road has been shut 450 days at day 3097 and 489 at day 3136.** Nobody goes up it in this block.
- **The practice mornings** are every day from 2611 to the dateline that is not a Thursday and not a Saturday. **The calendar count is 348 at day 3097 and 376 at day 3136, the count of mornings the practice was due on is 342 and 370, and the loss is six on every one of them.** The practice does not run on the five market mornings of this block's ten datelines and the page says so, **and it does run on the first of Longlight at day 3126, which is a Friday and not a market morning.**
- **The number** said out loud at the fourth hour is **four**, it was eight until nine days of water, and it has not gone back, and two of the ten things came back after the water and two have not.
- **The printed notice** was read at the boards on day 2665, the first of Mudmonth was day 2706, it passed with nothing enforced, **and it is three hundred and ninety-one days past its date at day 3097 and four hundred and thirty at day 3136 and has shut nothing.**
- **The roll** was nailed up on day 2827 and is **two hundred and seventy days on the boards at day 3097 and three hundred and nine at day 3136, with nine empty lines on each of three copies and the fourth line empty on all three.** **The sheet on the frame is a fifth thing and stays beside the roll and not over it, and its date is the twenty-ninth of Goatmonth YR 323, being day 3034, being sixty-three days past at day 3097 and one hundred and two at day 3136.**
- **The two refusals** of Volume 15 are days 2509 and 2521, and neither man is asked anything.
- **The brood** stands at five frames under about nine straw skirts and no sixth has gone in, and the young man of about nineteen has said out loud three things in that street in about four and a half years and nobody has asked him for an account of them. **Nothing is on the page about the skirts that a character has to act on, and nobody has been asked whether his trade is on one of the nine lines of the hand paper.**
- **The standing broom** is about nine hundred yards of a line nine feet wide and the water laid nearly all of it flat, and it will not close over.
- **The wall's gap** is about nine feet long and four feet high and the ninth yard has not been started, and the mallet is on the bank two miles off with the line of stone and is not picked up. **Four separate things in this county are about nine feet across, being this gap, the width of the made road, the width of the standing broom and the length of that dead line of grass, and a course of sill at the culvert is about nine feet long and a person lays about nine feet of kerb a week. Carry the noun with the number every time and never print the number on its own.**
- **The four lines of chalk** are on the stone sill of that weigh-house door **under the hood where the rain does not reach**, they mean four, nobody has read them out loud in about four and a half years, and the stick of chalk is in a press drawer and the man of about fifty-four has not asked for it.
- **The leaf at the back of that day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody**, and the day-book stands at eleven entries and the register holds ten questions with no finding under any of them.
- **The bleed** began on the fifth of Wolfmonth YR 323, being day 2920, and is **one hundred and seventy-seven days old at day 3097 and two hundred and sixteen at day 3136, and it has not faded and nobody in nine counties knows about it and it is in no document and it gets no panel and no explanation and no panel-shaped paragraph in any of these ten files.**
- **The hand lamp** goes on the coping at the low side of that causeway four days south every Monday afternoon in the winter, **and three of this block's ten datelines are Mondays, being 3101, 3108 and 3136, so a writer may put the lamp there on the afternoon of any one of those three and may not put it there on any of the other seven, and the page says the afternoon is the lamp's if it says it at all.**
- **The firsts of a month** are twenty-seventh at day 3126 and that one carries Chapter 0832, **and the count is not begun again.** The next two are twenty-eighth at day 3156 and first at day 3186, and the volume's last day is 3180, so only 3156 is inside this volume and it is outside this block.
